title: Pure Foundations — Algebra, Functions & Coordinate Geometry
subject: maths

questions.feedbackWrong: Square first: $4x^6$; then subtract exponents: $x^{6-4} = x^2$.

mistakes.correction: The power applies to everything inside the bracket: $2^2 = 4$, not 2.

mistakes.misconception: Multiplies exponents 6 × 4 instead of adding/subtracting for multiplication of powers.
mistakes.correction: When multiplying powers of the same base you ADD exponents — here $6 + (-4) = 2$.

questions.prompt: Using the factor theorem, confirm $(x-2)$ is a factor of $f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 6$ by evaluating $f(2)$. Enter the value of $f(2)$.
Prove that the sum of two consecutive odd numbers is always even.
questions.guidance: Write the numbers algebraically — e.g. $2n+1$ and $2n+3$.

markScheme.text: Represents two consecutive odd numbers algebraically, e.g. $2n+1$ and $2n+3$ for integer n.
Factorises: $4n + 4 = 4(n + 1) = 2 \times 2(n+1)$, showing the result is a multiple of 2.
Concludes explicitly: since n is any integer the result holds for ALL consecutive odd pairs — a proof, not examples.

mistakes.misconception: Verifies with numeric examples (3+5=8) and calls it proof.
mistakes.correction: Examples can support but never prove — a proof must cover every case algebraically.

questions.prompt: The graph of $y = f(x)$ is transformed to $y = f(x + 3)$. Which transformation is this?
options: Translation 3 units in the positive x-direction
Translation 3 units in the negative x-direction
Stretch factor 3 parallel to the x-axis
Translation 3 units in the positive y-direction
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — $f(x+a)$ shifts the graph LEFT by a.
questions.feedbackWrong: Inside-the-bracket changes act on x in the opposite direction: $f(x+3)$ moves the graph 3 units in the negative x-direction.

mistakes.misconception: Assumes +3 inside the bracket means positive x movement.
mistakes.correction: Transformations inside the function act in reverse: the graph reaches each output earlier, i.e. shifted left.
Changes outside the function affect y; changes inside affect x.

questions.prompt: Find the gradient of the line through $(2, 5)$ and $(6, 13)$.
A circle has equation $(x - 3)^2 + (y + 1)^2 = 25$. Write down its centre and radius, and determine whether the point $(6, 3)$ lies on the circle, showing your reasoning.

markScheme.text: Centre $(3, -1)$ read from the standard form — note the sign reversal on the y-coordinate.
Radius $= \sqrt{25} = 5$ — the right-hand side is $r^2$, not r.
Since it satisfies the equation (equals 25 exactly), the point lies ON the circle.

mistakes.misconception: Reads the right-hand side as the radius rather than its square.
mistakes.correction: The standard form is $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$ — so 25 is $r^2$ and $r = 5$.

mistakes.misconception: Misses the sign reversal on the y-coordinate of the centre.
mistakes.correction: $(y + 1)$ is $(y - (-1))$, so the y-coordinate of the centre is $-1$.

questions.prompt: The equation $x^2 + kx + 9 = 0$ has exactly one repeated real root. Explain how the discriminant determines this, and find the possible values of k.

markScheme.text: A repeated root occurs exactly when the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac = 0$.

mistakes.misconception: Takes only the positive square root.
mistakes.correction: $k^2 = 36$ has two solutions; a negative coefficient also produces a repeated root (at negative x).

questions.prompt: A line has gradient $\frac{2}{3}$. What is the gradient of any line perpendicular to it?
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — perpendicular gradients multiply to -1: negative reciprocal.
questions.feedbackWrong: Perpendicular gradient is the negative reciprocal: flip AND negate, giving $-\frac{3}{2}$.

mistakes.correction: Perpendicular lines satisfy $m_1 m_2 = -1$ — you must invert the fraction too.
Same-sign gradients with product +1 are not perpendicular; the product must be -1.
